facts.text: The Union government means the Central government.
facts.quote: The Union government means the Central government.

facts.text: The Union Government is made up of the President, the Legislature (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) and the Executive (Prime Minister and Council of Ministers).
facts.quote: Union Government ... President ... Legislature ... Executive ... Lok Sabha Rajya Sabha ... Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

facts.text: In a parliamentary system, the executive is part of the legislature and is responsible to the legislature.
facts.quote: In a parliamentary system, the executive is part of the legislature and is responsible to the legislature.

facts.text: India's Union Executive comprises the President, Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
facts.quote: India's Union Executive comprises of the President, Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.

facts.text: The President is the Supreme Head of the State; the office has the highest honour and prestige and represents the Republic of India.
facts.quote: the President is the Supreme Head of the State. The office of the President has the highest honour and prestige and it represents the Republic of India.

facts.text: All executive powers of the State are vested in the President by the Constitution, and the Government carries out its functions in the name of the President.
facts.quote: All executive powers of the State are vested in the President by the Constitution. The Government carries out its functions in the name of the President.

facts.text: In reality the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers run the government; the President is the nominal and constitutional head and the Prime Minister is the executive head.
facts.quote: However, in reality, the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers run the government. Therefore, the President is the nominal and constitutional head whereas the Prime Minister is the executive head.

facts.text: The Prime Minister informs the President about the administration of the country and about new laws and policies; the President has a right to seek such information.
facts.quote: The Prime Minister informs the President about the administration of the country and about new laws and policies. Rather, the President has a right to seek such information.

facts.text: The President is indirectly elected; common people do not vote; the directly elected representatives of the Central and State legislatures, known as the Electoral College, elect the President.
facts.quote: The President is indirectly elected by the people of India. The common people do not vote in the election of the President. He is elected by directly elected representatives of the Central and State legislatures. The group of these parliamentarians and members of the state legislatures is known as the Electoral College.

facts.text: The tenure of the President is five years.
facts.quote: The tenure of the President is five years.

facts.text: A person contesting the Presidential elections should be an Indian citizen who has completed 35 years of age.
facts.quote: The person contesting the Presidential elections should be an Indian citizen who has completed 35 years of age.

facts.text: The President takes an oath to protect the Constitution and ensure that the government runs as per the constitution.
facts.quote: According to the oath, the President bears the responsibility of protecting the Constitution and ensuring that the government runs as per the constitution.

facts.text: The President governs in accordance with the advice given by the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
facts.quote: The President governs in accordance with the advice given by the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.

facts.text: If any act of the President violates the Constitution, the Parliament can remove the President; this process is known as Impeachment.
facts.quote: But if any act of President violates the Constitution then the Parliament has the authority to remove the President. This process is known as process of Impeachment.

facts.text: In impeachment, any one House lays the charge, the other House investigates it, and the resolution must be passed by special (2/3rd) majority of both Houses.
facts.quote: Any one House can lay the charge of violation of the Constitution and the investigation of the charge is carried out by the other House. The resolution has to be passed by special (2/3rd) majority of both the Houses of Parliament.

facts.text: The President summons the meeting of Parliament, prorogues its session, sends messages to both Houses, and dissolves the Parliament after or even before the tenure is over.
facts.quote: The President summons the meeting of Parliament, prorogue the session of Parliament, sends messages to both Houses, dissolves the Parliament after the tenure is over or even before the tenure gets over.

facts.text: A Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha must be signed by the President; without his signature it cannot become a law.
facts.quote: Bill passed by the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha must be signed by the President. Without his signature, the Bill cannot become a law.

facts.text: The President appoints the Prime Minister and other ministers on the recommendation of the Prime Minister.
facts.quote: The President appoints the Prime Minister and other ministers on the recommendation of Prime Minister.

facts.text: The President appoints the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts, the Governors of States, the Chief Election Commissioner and other important officers.
facts.quote: The President appoints the judges of the Supreme Court and the High Courts. The President also appoints the Governors of States, Chief Election Commissioner and other important officers.

facts.text: The President is the supreme commander of the defence forces; decisions regarding war and peace are made by the President.
facts.quote: The President is the supreme commander of the defence forces. Decisions regarding war and peace are made by the President.

facts.text: The President has judicial powers: to reduce punishment, commute a sentence, or in special circumstances grant pardons or reprieves on humanitarian grounds.
facts.quote: the President has the power to reduce the punishment, grant a reduction in punishment or commute a sentence of a person or in special circumstances grant pardons or reprieves on humanitarian grounds.

facts.text: The President can declare emergency in a crisis; the Constitution mentions three kinds: National Emergency, State Emergency and Financial Emergency.
facts.quote: The President has the power to declare emergency in case of a crisis situation arising in the country. There are three kinds of emergencies mentioned in the Constitution. (1) National Emergency (2) State Emergency (3) Financial Emergency

facts.text: In the absence of the President, the Vice-President carries out his functions; the Vice-President is elected by members of both the houses of the Parliament.
facts.quote: In the absence of the President, his functions are carried out by the Vice-President. The Vice-President is elected by members of both the houses of the Parliament.

facts.text: The party which attains a majority nominates its leader as the Prime Minister; the Council of Ministers is formed of trustworthy colleagues from within the party.
facts.quote: The party which attains a majority in elections nominates their leader as the Prime Minister. The Council of Ministers is then formed of trustworthy colleagues from within the party.

facts.text: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers must be members of the parliament; if not, they must get elected to the Parliament within six months of their appointment.
facts.quote: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers must be members of the parliament. In case they are not members, they are required to get elected to the Parliament within six months of their appointment.

facts.text: The real executive powers are vested with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
facts.quote: This means that the real executive powers are vested with the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.

facts.text: The Prime Minister's foremost task is to form the Council of Ministers, giving priority to trustworthy colleagues considering administrative experience, governance skills, efficiency and subject expertise.
facts.quote: The foremost task of the Prime Minister is to form his Council of Ministers. While doing this, the Prime Minister gives priority to trustworthy colleagues while considering their administrative experience, governance skills, efficiency and subject expertise.

facts.text: After deciding the members of the council of ministers, the Prime Minister allocates portfolios to them.
facts.quote: After deciding upon the members of the council of ministers, the Prime Minister allocates portfolios to them.

facts.text: The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers and chairs all its meetings.
facts.quote: The Prime Minister leads the Council of Ministers. The Prime Minister chairs all the meetings of the Council of Ministers.

facts.text: The Prime Minister maintains coordination, facilitates cooperation and supervises the working of departments to maintain efficacy and efficiency.
facts.quote: the Prime Minister has to maintain coordination in the working of various departments, facilitate cooperation amongst the departments, supervise the working of these departments in order to maintain efficacy and efficiency etc.

facts.text: The Prime Minister also raises the image of the country in the international arena, develops trust among people and gives strong support to victims of any disaster.
facts.quote: to raise the image of the country in the international arena and work towards achieving a favourable opinion globally, to develop trust among people and to provide strong support to people who are victims of any disaster etc.

facts.text: The Council of Ministers takes initiative in the process of law-making; schemes and policy plans are drafted, discussed and then introduced in the House.
facts.quote: In a parliamentary form of government the Council of Ministers takes initiative in the process of Law-making. The scheme, policy plans etc. are drafted and discussed and then introduced in the House.

facts.text: Ministers lay their policy plans (on subjects like education, agriculture, industry, health, foreign relations) in Parliament for discussion and try to get them approved.
facts.quote: Education, agriculture, industry, health, foreign relations are subjects upon which the Council of Ministers has to decide specific policies ... the Ministers of respective departments lay their policy plans in the Parliament to bring about a discussion on it, and try to get it approved by the Parliament.

facts.text: Implementation of policy is the foremost responsibility of the Council of Ministers.
facts.quote: Implementation of policy is the foremost responsibility of the Council of Ministers. Once the Parliament approves the policies or draft proposals, the Council of Ministers implements them.

facts.text: 'Jumbo Ministry' means a huge Council of Ministers; a constitutional amendment limited ministers to not more than 15% of the total members of the Lok Sabha.
facts.quote: This refers to huge Council of Ministers. ... a constitutional amendment was made to limit the size of the Council of Ministers. As per this amendment, the number of ministers in the council should not be more than 15% of the total number of members in the Lok Sabha.

facts.text: Discussions and debates are an integral part of law-making; they help members scrutinise policy proposals and laws and point out shortcomings.
facts.quote: Debate and discussion among the members of the House are an integral part of the lawmaking process. These debates and discussions help the members to scrutinise the policy proposals and laws and point out the shortcomings.

facts.text: Question Hour: during sessions, proceedings begin with members' questions which ministers must answer satisfactorily; it is one of the most effective checks on the Council of Ministers.
facts.quote: During parliamentary sessions, the proceedings of the House begins with questions asked by the members of the House. The concerned ministers are supposed to give satisfactory answers to these questions. Question Hour is one of the most effective ways of keeping a check over the Council of Ministers.

facts.text: During question hour members criticise the government; occasionally members walk out or enter the well of the House and give slogans to protest.
facts.quote: During question hour, members criticise the government and ask questions on various issues. ... Occasionally, members walk-out of the House or enter into the well of the House and give slogans to record their protest.

facts.text: Zero Hour is the period around 12 noon during parliamentary sessions, when any question of public importance can be raised and discussed.
facts.quote: During the parliamentary sessions, the period around 12 noon is called 'Zero Hour'. During this period, any question of public importance can be raised and discussed.

facts.text: The government stays in power while it has majority support in the Lok Sabha; members move a no-confidence motion by saying 'we do not have confidence in the government', and if it passes the Council of Ministers must resign.
facts.quote: The government stays in power till it enjoys the support of majority in Lok Sabha. ... The members of the House can move a no-confidence motion by simply expressing 'we do not have confidence in the government'. If the motion is passed with majority support then the Council of Ministers has to resign.

facts.text: There is an extensive bureaucracy that works under the executive.
facts.quote: There is an extensive bureaucracy that works under the executive.
